verdict.rationale: Riveter documents large-scale, batch-oriented data gathering. Enrichments fill columns using web scrapes across up to 10,000 rows per /enrich request, a single request can fan out across a whole city's practices, and there is a standalone scrape endpoint. However, nothing documents concurrent scraping sessions as such: no parallelism controls, concurrency limits, or session model, and the SDK's handling of 429 retries implies rate limits whose levels are unstated. Missing for 10: documented concurrency/parallel-session limits, rate-limit or throughput figures for scraping, independent or hands-on corroboration of performance at scale.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can spin up many concurrent scraping sessions to gather data at scale

citations.quote: up to 10,000 rows per `/enrich` request with `enrichment_id`
An enrichment takes rows of input data and fills in new columns using AI, web searches, web scrapes, and other tools.
It can find every dental practice in a city, then pull every dentist from each one, in a single request.
A scrape lets you turn a URL into easily parseable text.
